current_activity: daylight drop into the 517th zone west of Le Muy at 1810, as planned
notes: Event date: 15 August 1944, 1810 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 6, p. 102). Event definition: The 1st Battalion, 551st Parachute Infantry, jumps without incident into the 517th regiment's drop zone from 1810, as planned (Clarke and Smith, ch. 6); Wikipedia puts the zone about two miles west of Le Muy. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 6, p. 103: "551st Parachute Infantry, jumped without incident into the 517th regiment's drop zone beginning at 1810, as planned"; Wikipedia, 1st Airborne Task Force: "The 1st Battalion, 551st Parachute Infantry Regiment would follow later in the day". Location: Le Muy, Var (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Le Muy; the zone was about two miles west of it. Location support: Clarke and Smith name the 517th zone, two miles west of Le Muy. Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

current_activity: clears most of Draguignan by 2300 and captures part of the LXII Corps staff
notes: Event date: 16 August 1944, by 2300 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 7). Event definition: The battalion sets out west for Draguignan, where elements of the LXII Corps headquarters still hold out, and by 2300 on 16 August has cleared most of the town and captured part of the corps staff and the German military governor of the Var (Clarke and Smith, ch. 7). Wikipedia dates the liberation of Draguignan 15 August. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 7, p. 118: "By 2300 on the 16th, the battalion had cleared most of the town and captured part of the corps staff"; Wikipedia, 551st Parachute Infantry Battalion: "They liberated Draguignan , France on 15 August 1944". Location: Draguignan, Var (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith and Wikipedia name Draguignan. Location caveat: Wikipedia gives 15 August; the official history's 16 August is used. Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

Location: Nice, Alpes-Maritimes (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Nice. Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

current_activity: arrives at Werbomont and enters the Battle of the Bulge with over 600 men
notes: Event date: 21 December 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: Moved from Laon on 19 December, the battalion arrives at Werbomont and enters the battle on 21 December with more than 643 men (Wikipedia). Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, 551st Parachute Infantry Battalion: "The 551st Parachute Infantry Battalion arrived in Werbomont , Belgium and entered the Battle of the Bulge on 21 December 1944". Location: Werbomont, Liège (PL0377) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Werbomont. Context: Relationship: the 1st Airborne Task Force attachment is closed on 21 November 1944, the day before Wikipedia's attachment to the 101st Airborne Division (inferred value). Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

current_activity: about 250 men attack Rochelinval over open ground without artillery support; Joerg killed
notes: Event date: 7 January 1945 (Wikipedia). Event definition: The remaining 250 men of the battalion are ordered on 7 January to attack the village of Rochelinval over open ground without artillery support; the commander, Lieutenant Colonel Joerg, is killed (Wikipedia); the 517th page puts the attached 551st in the 82nd Airborne attack along the Salm from 3 January. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, 551st Parachute Infantry Battalion: "the remaining 250 members of the battalion were ordered on 7 January 1945 to attack the Belgian village of Rochelinval"; Wikipedia, 517th Parachute Regimental Combat Team: "The 551st PIR, as an attached unit, fought through Basse-Bodeux". Location: Rochelinval, Liège (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Rochelinval. Commander: Lieutenant Colonel Wood G. Joerg, killed at Rochelinval on 7 January 1945 (Wikipedia, 551st Parachute Infantry Battalion). Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).
